20th People's Majlis

People's Majlis

Minutes of Committees of the People's Majlis

12th Meeting of the Judiciary Committee

20 October 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis (Committee Room 12)
Time started: 12:41

{Presiding: Chair of the Committee; Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed}

Chair speaking:
Assalaamu alaikum. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I welcome all honourable members to the 12th meeting of the Judiciary Committee of the People's Majlis. All honourable members have now received this committee's agenda. In that regard, I will say that mainly what is set on the agenda is setting the deadline for the two bills that most recently came to the committee, namely the amendment to the Criminal Procedure Code and the bill on proceeds of crime, and setting the deadline for advertising to open them for public opinion, and setting the deadline for completing the bills. Both of these bills, you know. In addition, the committee most recently extended the deadline of five bills until 15 October. The work on those five bills too, and the comments from the AG and PG have still not been received. As the administrative desk informed, when they took an update last week, they were informed that they are working jointly with the PG and the AG, and that they will send the comments very soon. Next, what is set on the agenda is a decision to be made regarding filing the reports of the decisions made by the Judicial Service Commission. In that regard, the reports already completed, along with summaries of these reports, will have been shared with the honourable members earlier in the group as well as now. So, to the floor, so, among the matters set on the agenda, first, the deadlines for the two bills under number one and opening them for public comment, I will open these matters to the honourable members on the floor to see what members think, you know. Thank you. So, I open the floor. Yes! I give the floor to the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh.

Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh speaking:
Thank you, Chair. For this bill, I propose for the two bills, the public, the bill on proceeds of crime, since this is a newly introduced bill. And along with that, this is the bill to amend Law No. 12/2016 (Criminal Procedure Code). To open this bill to seek public opinion

until the month of November, until 30 November of this year. And along with that, since it is a bill for which a great deal of important information needs to be obtained from relevant institutions, and from places very closely connected to the institutions, to open the work on these two bills until December to obtain information from institutions and organisations. In addition, the deadline for the bill, for both these bills, since this is a bill on which we will have to do a great deal of work within this committee, and there are very many things to ensure, and since it is a very important bill on which we believe I will have to do a great deal of work with the various relevant institutions and organisations, I propose, as I said, and also because the Majlis recess will come in between, to set the deadline for completing the work on the bill, completing the work on both bills, as the month of February. Of 2027, yes!

Chair speaking:
During these days we will also have to read both these bills on record, won't we. So, our work still remains. I just mentioned that for information. In the period ahead we will hold committee meetings and proceed with completing that part of both bills. So, if any other honourable member has another opinion, I would ask to proceed. Yes! I give the floor to Ashraf Rasheed, honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency.

Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed speaking:
Thank you, honourable Chair. I wish to say that I second the proposal as made by the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh.

Chair speaking:
I give the floor to Ibrahim Nazil, honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. I too second honourable member Mamdooh's proposal. At the same time, we are giving a lot of days, roughly forty days, to open this for public opinion. Along with that, as the committee proceeds with the work on this bill, is it after receiving public opinion that we will consult with the institutions related to this matter, at a somewhat later date? That is, the deadline now is until February, starting next year, starting from the session. Or will we meet when those opinions are received, when public opinion is received? Or, in between, the budget is coming, the People's Majlis budget. Will it be done during the budget, or will we postpone it like that since it may become a bit difficult? That is just a question that came to mind.

Chair speaking:
I think that if honourable members decide, for example, after we seek public opinion, it would also be sent to them, to the organisations, by the date set here, wouldn't it. Then, after seeking public opinion, if we need to summon them on a date in between, perhaps information could be clarified by summoning them. The other way is that once their comments are also received, looking at those too, I think summoning them and questioning them. By then we would have sufficient information in hand, wouldn't we. So, perhaps the best way is to hold it after the comments are received. Then, if members wish it that way, if decided that way, after the comments we will proceed by summoning the parties of the relevant organisations as well and obtaining information. Please continue.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
What the honourable Chair noted is that in the days we have, this committee, these two bills, one of the bills is a newly introduced bill. That bill on proceeds of crime. And the other is the amendment to the Criminal Procedure Code. As we read these two bills, some matters that we note

from various organisations to us, and also during the period we have opened for comments, and even before that, if there is something that needs to be brought to the committee in that way, or if there is something we want to clarify, I propose that we do that. By doing that. Then, when the Majlis opens in February and we work towards the deadline now set, it will be much easier for us. And we will also know very clearly what further things need to be done. So, I propose in that way that, as we proceed with the work on this bill, if we really need to question the parties connected to it, we keep the opportunity to do that.

Chair speaking:
I give the floor to Hassan Waheed, honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency.

Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed speaking:
Thank you, Chair. I too can second the proposal made by the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil. As we carry out this work, if we really need to question someone to resolve a confusion, whether by meeting with that party, or by summoning them to the committee, or by sending a letter, I also see clarifying those matters as the best way, so I second the honourable member's proposal. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Is there any further proposal? Or is there any further opinion now regarding these two bills? If not, we will put the proposals just made to a vote and then proceed with the next matter. So, I will call for the vote. I believe there are now two proposals. That is, the deadline dates proposed by the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, and the proposal made by Ibrahim Nazil on summoning organisations, which has been seconded. So,

first I will put to a vote what Mohamed Mamdooh, honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, has proposed: to open the amendment to Law No. 12/2016 (Criminal Procedure Code) and the bill submitted on proceeds of crime for public opinion until 30 November 2026, and to obtain comments from institutions, institutions, 30. Obtain comments from institutions until 30 December 2026. And that the work on the whole bill be completed by February 2027. So, I ask the honourable members who agree to decide in this way to vote. (Voting). Yes! Thank you. So, I declare this proposal passed with the unanimous consent of the honourable members present. Now the second proposal is the one proposed by the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, and seconded by the honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed: that as we carry out the work on this bill and as the articles of the bill are read in the committee, if it becomes really necessary to summon the parties of an organisation in connection with that matter, they be summoned. So, if it is agreed to summon them that way, to summon the relevant parties of that organisation, I ask the honourable members who agree to vote. (Voting). Yes! So, I announce that this proposal too has passed in this way. Next, set under number two of the agenda: we most recently set the deadline of five bills to 15 October. These are the amendment to the Penal Code of the Maldives submitted on behalf of the government by the Member for Maafushi constituency, and the amendment to Courts Law 22/2010 (Judicature Act of the Maldives) that I submitted, and the amendment to the Penal Code of the Maldives submitted by the honourable Member for South Galolhu constituency, Meekail Ahmed Nasym, and the amendment to the Evidence Act submitted on behalf of the government by the Member for Bilehdhoo constituency, Ahmed Aslam, and the amendment bill to the Penal Code submitted on behalf of the government by the Member for Central Hithadhoo constituency, Ahmed Azaan Marzooq. For these too, comments have not yet been received from government organisations, you know. Administratively, they are checking by calling from this end. They are working on it. According to them, the work is progressing. Then

but they have not been received yet. So that is why we have to extend this. So, what do the honourable members think about this? And how many more days do you think should be given? Yes! I give the floor to Mohamed Mamdooh, honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency.

Member for North Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh speaking:
Thank you, Chair. I too will have had some kinds of consultations on this matter with some of the institutions related to it. And this matter will also have been discussed. In reality, the reason some of the comments this committee needs have not been received is that there are very many things these parties need to ensure in these bills. And in reality they are carrying out the work that has to be done jointly, one institution with another, one office with another. However, very many things have to be ensured and very many things have to be looked at. In reality these are bills for which they themselves need comments from very many directions. In reality these amendments, these bills that have been submitted, are very sensitive. So, when amendments are brought to such bills, to such laws, in reality they are taking time to ensure that nothing at all is left out from any direction. That is very clear to me. So, Chair, I think it is right to set again a good period as the deadline for these bills. As I believe, these two places, two offices, have jointly done very important work specifically on these bills even during the past week. Very important consultations have also been held. So, as I believe, along with these consultations, I think in reality it is reasonable to give them a good, adequate period to send the comments these parties have to send. I think, for example, considering the period in which the Majlis goes ahead, the budget matters come, and the Majlis goes on recess, to set the deadline for these bills

accordingly. In reality, in order to give them room to carry out this matter as completely as possible for the comments, I propose 30 November as the deadline for all these bills.

Chair speaking:
I give the floor to the honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, Mauroof Zakir. I give the floor to Ibrahim Nazil, honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Thank you, Chair. I, just five bills, right. How long has it been, the bills. Now, at the end of the day, at the very last moment, it will turn out that this committee was unable to do this, you know. It will turn out that the Judiciary Committee of the People's Majlis received the bill, the bill stayed here, and after eight months, nine months, this committee could not do it. So, like that, has that been discussed? Otherwise it will turn out that it was not done. So, if we do not deal with this matter a bit more seriously, other institutions may remain very relaxed. Even before this, when some time passes in this committee, this is often how things go. So, unless the honourable Chair in particular deals with this matter somewhat firmly, it will just go on drifting like this, you know. We should not give away that opportunity like that and remain labelled by it. The government sends bills only because the government really wants to do them. The related institutions keeping it that way may also be for some other purpose. It is not clear to us. We need to make a decision on this. If they do not send comments, I think we need to complete it with the bill we have received and send it, we need to finish it. Just that point at this opportunity. And in addition, as honourable member Mamdooh noted, once November falls within this, we will not be able to proceed in any way other than next year. So, it just came to my mind that we want to share this at committee level, you know. Then, by the committee making a decision, together with the government

consulting and speeding up the things that can be sped up, since I see that as the best way. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
The honourable member made a good point, you know. Then, from the administrative desk, we check how their work and replies and so on are coming in. They say they are working on it. Then, you will know that among these, there is honourable member Meekail, who has submitted an amendment to the Penal Code, right. And a law related to it has also come. At that time it was delayed because, given that law, the AG advised that when amending the Land Transport Act, some of the penalties set out in it would be included in the law, so to hold off on amending it first. We may be able to get advice on that. Then actually, once every two weeks or once a week, at the administrative desk, I mean by telling the administrative staff, we check how it is going? Are the comments coming? At what stage is it, to work on it. Then, as you said, nevertheless, completing it quickly is a responsibility of ours, you know. I give the floor to Mauroof Zakir, honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency. After that, to Shamin, you know.

Member for Kendhoo constituency, Mauroof Zakir speaking:
Shamin can be given the floor first if he wishes. Thank you, honourable Chair. Now this is actually a matter we should be very concerned about. As the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency just noted, tomorrow we will see some members of the public come out and make a petition to cut the committee allowance. This is what happens when it is like this. Work is assigned to the committee, the committee allowance is given. However, a committee is unable to fulfil this responsibility. When the Judiciary Committee too is under a government minister or a ministry, the public will see a picture of this committee being unable to work. At that point the public will come out and make a petition. Making petitions is now very common. So, they will make a petition

and submit it to the Majlis to cut the allowance. Isn't it right to submit it if we cannot do that work? I think, instead of writing to the relevant offices and ministries to obtain comments, they should be told to attend this committee on such-and-such a day with the comments. Then they would have to come here together with the comments. The People's Majlis has entrusted us with big responsibilities, and moreover we are talking about important bills. So, they should be told to attend together with the comments. And if we cannot do even that much, we should just sit debating petitions. Bringing petitions, bringing petitions to the committee, then sending petitions, then bringing petitions, we should sit debating petitions. Nothing else can be done. So, I propose that this be changed in that way. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
I give the floor to the honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, Mohamed Shamin Habeeb. Kurendhoo, honourable Member for Kurendhoo constituency. Sorry.

Member for Kurendhoo constituency, Mohamed Shamin Habeeb speaking:
Thank you, Chair. I too second the comments of the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, and the honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, Mauroof Zakir. The reason is that these are bills that have been with us for a very long time. If we are seeking someone's opinion by sending it, we need to give a deadline to obtain it. Then I think the solution to this is to summon those people and proceed in that way. Otherwise we will keep on checking forever. However much the administrative desk checks, what will come to us from that end is a computer reply. I do not believe the work here should come to a halt because someone is being slow. That is why, if a deadline is given and the work cannot be done by that deadline, the ones who have to be held responsible for it, it is we who have to be held responsible. What has been seen so far is that, often, just as we complete the work, a bunch of comments will arrive. We will have to complete it without even looking at those properly,

and pass it. So, that is not a way we want to work either. That is why, going forward, I really believe that, as the honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, Mauroof Zakir, proposed, a deadline be given and someone from that ministry come here together with the comments. Otherwise I do not think anyone will take responsibility for that work; from all parties, many places, because of just one party, we have to keep the bills pending. That is why my proposal is that this committee set that kind of principle. I am saying what I think. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
I give the floor to the honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed.

Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed speaking:
Thank you, honourable Chair. Yes! In connection with the matter now being discussed, I too wanted to say something. That is, in reality, bills are sent to the Majlis by the government. They are sent in a way that facilitates what is needed to bring the legal solutions that really must be brought in connection with the problems faced at that time. However, before a bill is passed by the Majlis, the work needed to complete the procedures that must be completed has to be done from various directions. So, among the bills now submitted to the Judiciary Committee, especially regarding the bills being discussed today, when we need further information, we are getting delayed because we have not received information that has to be brought through the very parties that sent the bill. So, in that case, those parties should work even harder than us to speed this up. So, when a law has been submitted, if a conflict arises because another law connected to that law is submitted to the Majlis, it is only once all of that is resolved and the laws are passed that the law will bring us the benefit it is meant to. So, that is what I believe. Then

what all the members have said, as a matter of principle, are very good points. If the Judiciary Committee delays these bills, the public will see it that way. However, the delay for these reasons is not something the Judiciary Committee does in order to delay it. So, the bills are sent by the government. We members submit to the Majlis the bills sent by the government. So, comments have to be obtained from those parties on the problems in those bills and on problems that may arise further. When the opportunity to submit comments has been opened and the delay is because comments have not come, that is not our problem. But if it is delayed, we on the committee side should do the work needed to speed it up. According to the information we receive, they are carrying out the work. So, honourable, I wish to say that I second the proposal made by the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh. I also respect what all the other members have said. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
I give the floor to Ibrahim Nazil, honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! Thank you, honourable Chair. What we are saying is that a bill comes to us after, in connection with matters related to that government ministry, consultation with the Attorney General, or after the government does it under the established procedure, the bill goes to the President's Office, the President's legal team also reviews the bill, and then the bill comes from the President's Office to us. This is the route it comes by. In that regard, after a bill comes, all those matters related to this bill, in reality the Attorney General's Office knows, they have arranged all of it: the amendments to be brought to laws and the new laws coming. So, conflicts between that bill and another bill and all these matters

should in reality be known beforehand. What I am saying is that bills submitted this year, in January 2026, are still here. This year is over. It is falling into next year. Meanwhile, with that bill lying in this Judiciary Committee of the People's Majlis, and so much time passing without us being able to work on it, must we just sit there, must we keep waiting because some other related matter at the Attorney General's Office is not finished. In reality, what I am saying is that we ask even for the Attorney General's advice: if there is some other related matter to decide, bring that decision to us within a very short period. We set a deadline for that purpose. Do it within that deadline. However, I am talking about things that have not moved forward from January until today. So, in this matter we need to, if they really do not send it, we can do this in this committee. I am talking about the things we can do in this committee by consulting and working with the administrative staff and the Majlis's legal staff. We should in no way have to keep this sitting because a particular party did not do this for us. And then again, if an amendment needs to be brought to it, won't the government send the amendment to it again? Isn't that so. Don't amendments come? Amendments come even before many days have passed. We are the ones here to make those amendments. That is our job. So, let us not keep it [?] here in a way that brings disrepute on our heads because it stayed in the committee so long and the committee could not do it. If a deadline is set, work to finish within that deadline. There are also situations where it does not get finished. However, because such a long period is passing, that is actually why I am saying it. In no way, because of one party or another, one party pointing a finger at another; let us get on with our committee's work. Let us, the members of this Judiciary Committee, proceed in this matter by fulfilling the responsibility of the Judiciary Committee. If we all go together with one voice to do that work in a united way, we can do it. There will be nothing we cannot do. We have the opportunity to do it. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Yes! Thank you. Looking at what the honourable member said, there are now matters in committees that have been pending for a very long time, right. For example, in this committee too, and some things submitted before our term also may remain unpassed and unfinished. However, what I am trying to say is, look for example at the Evidence Act, you know. The amendment to the Evidence Act bill came only the other day. It was sent. Then there are two or three amendments to the Penal Code under way. And there is also an amendment submitted to the Courts Act. So, looking at what you just said and these matters, there are some matters for which the committee may be able to find ways. So, we will work to reduce the backlog. However, as I said, I too accept that there are delays in comments coming from places like the PG and the AG. So we will work to see whether we can proceed by calling them or summoning them, in that way. And even outside this committee, there are matters pending for a very long time, aren't there, even outside this committee. Even though it is said like that, that we cannot do the committee's work, our work is indeed progressing. For example, I also note that by holding committee sessions every month and by attending administratively, the work we have to do has been done on previous bills too, with the cooperation of all members. However, taking into account the proposals you made, if you advise, we will work to see whether we can proceed. So, another honourable member, yes! I will give the floor, before Hassan, honourable member Ahmed Riyaz there has asked for the floor, you know. Ahmed Riyaz, please proceed! Honourable Member for Thimarafushi constituency.

Member for Thimarafushi constituency, Ahmed Riyaz speaking:
Thank you, Chair. Yes! As all the members just said, in reality what the general public will see is a picture of us in the Judiciary Committee having failed by not working, this

if things are not completed. That is a very good point. As we look at it, I generally note on the front page of every bill the deadlines and so on. Noting them, at the sitting we held on 5 January this year, we had decided that day to send the letters too. So, as I believe, in reality what we should have received should have been received by now. As Nazil just said, let us complete our work. He also mentioned the route it comes by, right. Even though he is a person far more senior than me and of a different thinking from ours. So, in reality it comes by that route, right. So, what comes here is something they have thought through as much as they can and prepared. So, let us, at a time when we do not receive further public comments, even by passing the bill as it is, let us save our responsibility from our heads. Then it will move forward, right. I believe the country will move forward then. So, I too think we should work without keeping it filed away.

Chair speaking:
I give the floor to the honourable Member for Milandhoo constituency, Hassan Mufeed.

Member for Milandhoo constituency, Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir speaking:
Yes! Thank you, honourable Chair. Regarding the views and consultation being debated among us, and the AG's comments, the comments of organisations, and opening for public opinion, it occurs to me whether we have to obtain these things by force. Sometimes it may be that they have no comment to make on this bill. In that case, I regard proceeding with our work within our mandate as a sensible thing. So, the AG may sometimes have no comment to make. Or the most relevant organisations may have no further opinion on this matter. I say that because, logically, I believe that when the AG drafts a bill too, they will consult to some extent with the

relevant parties. So, some amount of time has been given for that. So, when it is opened for public opinion, I do not believe that not receiving public opinion is something for which we have to extend the time and remain dependent on it. So, once we have opened this for comment for an adequate period and submitted to the AG and the other organisations most relevant to this matter to obtain their information, it not coming is another matter. So, I just wanted to say that. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Yes! So, with there being no further proposal, what is proposed by the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh, and seconded, now seconded by the honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed, is to set the deadline for these five bills now as 30 November 2026. So, I ask the honourable members who agree to that to vote. (Voting) Yes! So, I declare that proposal passed. Next now are the reports summarised by the administrative desk regarding filing the decisions made by the Judicial Service Commission, you know. As I said earlier, these reports will have been shared with the honourable members. If the honourable members do not note any issue, once it is decided to file these reports, the matters set for today are complete. So, I will give the floor to the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, you know.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Thank you, Chair. I too looked at those reports. Since I do not see that this committee necessarily needs to make any changes to the reports, I propose that we in the committee decide to file them just as they are.

Chair speaking:

I give the floor to the honourable Member for Thimarafushi constituency, Hassan Waheed. Honourable Member for Vilifushi, you know. Sorry! Honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed.

Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed speaking:
Yes! Chair. I second the proposal of the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil.

Chair speaking:
So, since the honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed, has seconded the proposal made by the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, that there is no problem with the reports now on the agenda, this; I give the floor to the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Thank you, Chair. Among the cases we just mentioned, there is 12/2022, complainant: Judicial Service Commission. Respondent: Magistrate Ziyad Thohir of the S. Hithadhoo Magistrate Court. Apart from that case, as I said earlier, since it is noted that we do not now need to make changes to the remaining cases, and since in the case just noted there are some documents we need to obtain further from the JSC, I propose that this committee keep that case pending and decide the remaining cases as they are.

Chair speaking:
I will give the floor to Mohamed Mamdooh, honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency.

Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh speaking:

Thank you, Chair. I wish to say that I second what the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency proposed: that we keep pending the case lacking documents and file all the remaining cases.

Chair speaking:
Yes! So, I will put it to a vote. I ask the honourable members who agree, as proposed by the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, and seconded by the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh, that, with there being no problem in the remaining reports apart from the report just excluded, those reports be filed, to vote. (Voting) Yes! Thank you. So, I declare it passed in that way with the unanimous consent of the members present. Since nothing else is set on the agenda today, I declare the committee meeting concluded at this point. Thank you, you know.
method: Translated by Claude from the Dhivehi transcription
